sources: Natural History Museum (London), How dangerous are false widow spiders?: looks similar to the more dangerous black widows with a similar dark, globular body; the pattern on its back is often described as skull-shaped; usually the only symptom of a bite is pain at the site which may radiate, ordinarily lasting one to 12 hours, no worse than a wasp sting; first recorded in the UK in the 1870s, probably a stowaway from its native Madeira and Canary Islands, strong foothold only since the 1980s; body length 7-14 mm, females larger; indoors often in kitchens and conservatories; webs usually at least 1.5 m off the ground; https://www.nhm.ac.uk/discover/how-dangerous-are-false-widow-spiders.html

University of Galway (NUI Galway) Venom Systems Lab, May 2021, New study confirms noble false widow spider bites can result in hospitalisation (Dunbar et al., Clinical Toxicology, https://doi.org/10.1080/15563650.2021.1928165): some victims have symptoms very similar to true black widow bites and some severe cases require hospitalisation; only cases with a clear identification of the spider were used, some confirmed by DNA; most cases have a mild outcome; https://universityofgalway.ie/about-us/news-and-events/news-archive/2021/may/new-study-confirms-noble-false-widow-spiders-bites-can-result-in-hospitalisation.html

University of California Statewide IPM Program, Pest Notes: Black Widow and Other Widow Spiders: adult female has a shiny black body and a red or orange hourglass on the underside of the large round abdomen; hangs upside down in an irregular, tough, sticky cobweb in dark, sheltered places such as wood piles and garages; males are one-half to two-thirds the length of the female; death from a bite is very unlikely; https://ipm.ucanr.edu/PMG/PESTNOTES/pn7442.html
MedlinePlus (U.S. National Library of Medicine), Black widow spider bite: muscle pain spreading from the bite, painful cramps, sweating; https://medlineplus.gov/ency/article/002858.htm

beats.say: The shiny black spider in your kitchen looks just like a black widow.
It's a noble false widow. And the pattern on its back looks like a skull.
In Ireland, scientists found some of its bites put people in the hospital.
But most bites are mild. Pain like a wasp sting, gone within half a day.
Now the real black widow. Shiny black, with a red hourglass under its belly.
Its venom hits your nerves. Painful cramps, and sweating. But death is very unlikely.
So the spider with a skull on its back is the less dangerous one.
